This cohort has 256 independent test episodes per condition; snapshots and queries are averaged within each episode.

results/main/beamforming/noise_adaptatio.selection_rationale: Shows the declared noise-change intervention and causal variance learning.
results/main/beamforming/noise_adaptatio.proposed_latex_caption: Causal variance learning under the predeclared noise-change intervention. Fits use completed, nonoverlapping past blocks and affect future variances only; every observation is assimilated once. Variance bands describe interquartile repeated-episode spread, not a posterior over the variance. Future-task and excluded-observation score intervals are pointwise 95\% intervals across independent episodes. Empirical-Bayes plug-in scales omit scale uncertainty and are outside the fixed-variance theorem. Motion and signal-power interventions remain supplementary.
results/main/beamforming/noise_adaptatio.full_source_caption: Actual causal variance learning from completed nonoverlapping past blocks. Each observation is corrected once; a fit updates only subsequent variances while retaining the streamed subspace belief. Known coordinate changes are aligned before block fitting. Curves show saved trajectory/episode summaries; variance bands are interquartile repeated-episode spread, not a posterior over variance. Future-task and pre-observation score intervals are pointwise 95\% intervals across independent episodes. Each page retains one predeclared noise-, motion-, or signal-power intervention. The contact supplementary density pages show one predeclared episode: panels (a,b) of the first density page use $t=32,96$, and panel (a) of the following density page uses $t=192$; pre-correction $A_t^-$ is converted to the wrist-frame normal law $q_{-A_t^-}$ with normalizer $\psi_1(-A_t^-)=\psi_2(A_t^-)-\operatorname{tr}(A_t^-)$. The three orthographic spheres share a density scale; panel (b) of the following density page shows the physical-query risk at all three checkpoints, $v_t^T(M_t^--(M_t^-)^2)v_t$ at the recorded physical query. This is individual belief uncertainty, distinct from the repeated-episode variance bands and from calibration. Empirical-Bayes plug-in scales omit their uncertainty and are outside the fixed-true-variance theorem.

results/main/beamforming/computation_tim.proposed_latex_caption: Warmed single-thread time to process exactly 64 observations. Optional uncertainty reports and variance fits occur every 32 observations, separately from the task-decision interval. EM uses the stated two or four iterations. Sums of per-operation medians need not equal the median total elapsed time. Repeated clocks measure execution variability on one data set, not additional statistical episodes or worst-case deadlines. Memory accounting is retained on the supplementary second page.
results/main/beamforming/computation_tim.full_source_caption: Time to process exactly 64 observations on one BLAS thread. Panel (a) includes all 64 parameter corrections and task decisions every one or sixteen observations; its displayed curves exclude optional uncertainty reports. Panel (b) separates parameter updates, task decisions, uncertainty reports, EM and other time for the same 64-observation workload. Row labels state task-decision intervals; optional uncertainty reports and EM fits occur every 32 observations. EM rows use two or four iterations. Phase stacks sum per-phase medians and need not equal median total elapsed time. The separate memory page distinguishes stored arrays from tracked allocations and excludes unmeasured native workspaces/RSS. Repeated clocks measure execution variability on a fixed statistical state, not independent task-performance episodes or worst-case deadlines.

results/main/contact/task_performance.pd.selection_rationale: Shows response MSE and confidence intervals for the posterior mean and same-data modal, isotropic and regularized-projector controls.
results/main/contact/task_performance.pd.proposed_latex_caption: Physical contact response MSE on independent episodes and common query streams. Panel (a) uses the stationary concentrated-input condition; its posterior-mean curve carries a pointwise 95\% confidence band. Panel (b) shows absolute episode-average MSE for the moving sphere condition, with pointwise 95\% intervals for every displayed method, including $\overline P_t^+$, $P_{\widehat{\mathcal X}_t}$, the matched isotropic mean $\overline P_t^{\mathrm{iso}}$, and the regularized projector. The isotropic control preserves mode and mean overlap; the regularized projector is $\rho P_{\widehat{\mathcal X}_t}+(1-\rho)(2/3)I_3$ with independently validated $\rho$. Query and time losses are averaged within each episode before intervals are formed. Paired MSE differences are retained on the supplementary second page; differences and absolute MSE both have squared velocity units, whereas relative MSE would be a ratio. GREAT has different input information, stated outside its figure label. Full reference and condition grids remain supplementary.
results/main/contact/task_performance.pd.full_source_caption: Task losses on common independent test episodes. Losses are averaged within each episode before pointwise Student 95\% intervals. For contact, main panel (a) shows stationary concentrated-input checkpoint MSE versus observation count, with the posterior-mean confidence band; panel (b) shows absolute episode-average MSE for the moving sphere condition, with a confidence interval for every method including the posterior mean. All methods in panel (b) use the same independent episodes. The separate second page retains paired MSE differences; these are absolute differences in squared velocity units, not relative MSE. A posterior mean compared with itself has identically zero paired difference. Beamforming paired boxes show the distribution of same-episode differences, not confidence intervals. GREAT and application-specific controls retain their stated information and independently validated settings. Complex beamforming GREAT is an extension of the real algorithm, as described in the notebook text. Oracle quantities are evaluation-only. This cohort has 256 independent test episodes per condition; snapshots and queries are averaged within each episode.

results/main/contact/posterior_anisotrop.proposed_latex_caption: The actual normal-line density $q_{-A_t^+}([n])$ at the fixed concentrated-input checkpoint $t=16$, and its fitted isotropic Bingham law with equal mode and mean squared chordal distance. The mean matrices are denoted by $\overline P_t^+$ and $\overline P_t^{\mathrm{iso}}$, following the supplement. Both unit-sphere views retain the saved coordinates, camera and shared logarithmic density normalization; antipodal normals represent the same plane. The blue--purple--pink--yellow gradient changes only the color mapping. For $v(\theta)=\cos\theta e_2+\sin\theta e_3$ and $\theta$ in radians, the lower panel evaluates $v(\theta)^\top[\overline P-(\overline P)^2]v(\theta)$ with each indicated belief and its own mean $\overline P$. These are posterior expected clean-response errors under different beliefs, rather than two estimators evaluated against one common truth. Practical comparisons use the separate repeated-episode task study. The constructed equal-distance-law example is supplementary.
results/main/contact/posterior_anisotrop.full_source_caption: actual data-generated $q_{-A_t^+}([n])$ and a fitted isotropic Bingham law with equal mode and mean squared chordal distance. Their fixed-radius orthographic views share camera and color normalization; antipodal normals represent one plane. Color clips only display resolution below its logarithmic floor. Panels (a) and (b) show the actual and fitted-isotropic laws; the orange marker identifies the visible representative of their common modal line. Panel (c) uses $v(\theta)=\cos\theta\,e_2+\sin\theta\,e_3$ and plots $v(\theta)^T(M-M^2)v(\theta)$ using each law and its own mean $M$. These are belief-specific predictive risks, not losses of two estimators evaluated against one common truth. A separate constructed swapped-eigenvalue page has identical centered chordal-distance laws but different directional risks. The actual posterior is the predeclared concentrated-input episode 0 at t=16. Visible anisotropy and repeated-experiment task benefit are separate comparisons. Spheres retain the original saved physical/coefficient coordinates and shared oblique camera. The blue-purple-pink-yellow palette uses the unchanged shared logarithmic density scale; its four-decade display floor does not mean zero density. Color positions are not probability quantiles. Thin gray curves are front-visible coordinate great circles, not density contours or credible regions. No mode-facing rotation, density deformation or additional posterior fitting is used. In the directional-risk panel, theta is in radians and the indicated mean is either the full posterior mean or the manuscript-defined isotropic mean; each curve is its own belief risk.

results/main/contact/information.pdf.selection_rationale: Shows which physical normal rotations the saved applied inputs distinguish, using the exact Gaussian likelihood divergence.
results/main/contact/information.pdf.proposed_latex_caption: Which normal rotations the original saved concentrated-input experiment distinguishes. At the generating plane, $n_0=e_3$, $X_0=(e_1,e_2)$ and $z=\operatorname{vec}(Z)$. The graph chart has normal $n(Z)=(n_0-X_0z)/\sqrt{1+\|z\|^2}$. With the same 16 prescribed inputs and true measurement variance, $p_Z$ is the joint Gaussian velocity law at this plane. Panel (a) shows equal values of its exact divergence $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p_0\|p_Z)=z^\top\mathcal F_{\mathrm{cond}}z/[2(1+\|z\|^2)]$. Panel (b) uses the physical normal angle $\delta$ along the two native information directions: rotations of $5^\circ$ and $30^\circ$ yield nearly equal divergences, approximately $0.24$. This connects directional excitation to distinguishability of physical rotations. Near zero the formula gives the manuscript Fisher expansion. The generating plane is used for this theoretical analysis, not supplied to the estimator. The contours are likelihood divergences, not posterior credible regions; no new observations, fitting or independent experimental repetitions are introduced.
results/main/contact/information.pdf.full_source_caption: Directional likelihood information for the original concentrated-input contact fixture at $t=16$. The generating normal is $n_0=e_3$, $X_0=(e_1,e_2)$, and the plane graph chart has $z=\operatorname{vec}(Z)=(z_1,z_2)^T$ and normal $n(Z)=(n_0-X_0z)/\sqrt{1+\|z\|^2}$. For the same frozen prescribed inputs and true variance, $p_Z$ is the joint Gaussian response law with means $P_{\mathcal X(Z)}v_j$ and covariance $\sigma^2I_3$. Panel (a) shows equal values of the exact divergence $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p_0\|p_Z)=z^T\mathcal F_{\mathrm{cond}}z/[2(1+\|z\|^2)]$ in native chart coordinates, with equal axis scales. These are likelihood-divergence contours, not credible or confidence regions. Panel (b) evaluates the same divergence along the two native information directions; $\delta$ is the physical angle between $n_0$ and $n(Z)$. The marked rotations $5^\circ$ and $30^\circ$ produce nearly equal divergences, approximately $0.2396$ and $0.2308$, despite their different angular sizes. Thus this input design distinguishes rotations much more strongly in one direction. The local limit is $D_{\mathrm{KL}}=\tfrac12z^T\mathcal F_{\mathrm{cond}}z+o(\|z\|^2)$. This is expected observation-law information at the generating plane, distinct from finite-data posterior curvature. No new observations, inference, fitting, or experimental repetitions are introduced.

results/supplementary/contact/predictive.proposed_latex_caption: Actual-recursion calibration with distinct state, clean-response and noisy-next-observation targets. Pages separate joint prior-predictive sampling, fixed-state repetitions and drift diagnostics. Vertical intervals are pointwise exact binomial uncertainty across independent episodes, not credible uncertainty. All intervals are evaluated at their declared time before the scored future observation is seen. Appended pages show 95% report-size distributions at t=64 for every probability regime. State-ball sizes are chordal radii, obtained by taking the square root of each recorded squared-distance upper threshold; HPD energy thresholds are not used as geometric widths. Scalar sizes are upper minus lower in the n=3 fixture units. Boxes show the median and interquartile range across independent episodes, with 1.5-IQR whiskers and every outlier; this spread is not a posterior distribution or a confidence interval over width. Proper-score checks are separate. Validation-fitted widths do not establish a matched-coverage advantage if achieved test coverage misses its target. results/supplementary/contact/paper_summ.proposed_latex_caption: Selected main panels from the same saved arrays used by the individual figures. Contact emphasizes the physical input/constraint model and directional posterior uncertainty; beamforming emphasizes moderate-dimensional task performance, causal variance learning and computational cost with matched task-decision intervals. No simulation, posterior resampling, tuning or trajectory selection occurs during summary composition. Caption conditions and full numerical records remain in the associated figure entries. Spheres retain the original saved physical/coefficient coordinates and shared oblique camera. The blue-purple-pink-yellow palette uses the unchanged shared logarithmic density scale; its four-decade display floor does not mean zero density. Color positions are not probability quantiles. Thin gray curves are front-visible coordinate great circles, not density contours or credible regions. No mode-facing rotation, density deformation or additional posterior fitting is used. In the directional-risk panel, theta is in radians and the indicated mean is either the full posterior mean or the manuscript-defined isotropic mean; each curve is its own belief risk.
